CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  May 3, 2021 - 4:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoco nference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the meeting to order at 4:31 p.m. The pledge
  of allegiance was led by Vice Mayor Wilson.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
  Council members:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Chief of Police John Perez introduced and welcomed the new
  Sergeant-at-Arms, Sergeant Milton White, and extended
Councilmember Hampton  appreciation to Sergeant Mark Mendenhall for his service.
connected to the meeting at
4:35 p.m.  Michelle Perera, Director of Library and Information Services,
  presented a PowerPoint presentation on the various virtual events
  and programs the library is participating in recognizing Asian
  American and Pacific Islander Heritage Month.

PUBLIC COMMENT  The following individuals expressed concerns with the Pasadena
  Police Department and Police Officers; requested the termination
  of Pasadena Police Chief Perez and Officer Dumaguindin; and
  spoke on the need for alternatives to policing measures in the City,
  including certain social services:

  Sara Boland, Los Angeles resident
  Jane Ward, Altadena resident
  Allen Shay, Pasadena resident

  Councilmember Kennedy requested a closed session update on
  two cases involving Pasadena Police Officers; Christopher Ballew
  and Anthony McClain.

  Mayor Gordo responded that both those matters are scheduled for
  a future closed session of the City Council meeting.

Council Minutes  1  05/03/2021
   Jill Shook, representing Making Housing and Community Happen,
  advocated for the City Council to rezone land owned by churches
  and other religious organizations to allow for building and providing
  affordable housing.

  Vice Mayor Wilson and Councilmember Hampton asked staff to
  work on an expedited time frame to return to the City Council with
  a recommendation on some aspect of rezoning land owned by
  churches and other religious organizations to allow for building and
  providing affordable housing.

  Councilmember Hampton stated the following for the record: "I
  would just like to go on the record, mentioning again and I will say
  this every City Council meeting, I do think that we need to agendize
  what we can about the Christopher Ballew matter, of course in
  closed [session]. As well as the Anthony McClain matter in closed
  [session]. But whatever we could disclose in public record, at the
  Public Safety [Committee] meeting, there should be an opportunity
  for the community to voice their opinion. I do not, once again, agree
  with the Police Chief's assessment and that the officers were acting
  appropriately. Once again I am not a police officer, so that is their
  assessment. I do want to say that when matters like this happen,
  over and over and over again, and then you put the same officers
  back to patrol the streets in the same community or the same
  people out there, that's creating the cycle of terror. And so, I don't
  want to act as if I am complacent in that in any way, so I am going
  to say what I have to say publicly every time regardless if this has
  to be at every [City] Council meeting, here on out. I normally hold
  these comments to Public Safety [Committee meetings], but we
  have to really look at this in a holistic manner. Because at the end
  of the day, these are our residents, and our residents should feel
  safe in the place that they live in. Not only by the people who work
  for the City, but also safe in the communities that they live in from
  their own neighbors. So, I think holding people accountable across
  the board is great, find and dandy; and I'm all for that. But when
  our employees, City employees, do wrong we need to hold them
  accountable. Thank you."

  Dear Mayor Gordo and Staff,

  I am officially requesting that the process for nomination for
  appointment to the Redistricting Task Force, which is essentially to
  empower 3 additional Mayoral appointments, be tabled from the
  City Council Consent Calendar of 3 May 2021 so that a much
  needed public discussion can take place and the City Council can
  jointly determine the process.

  Some of my concerns are as follows:

  1. The process the Mayor has undertaken is different from the
  process that the City Council undertook to appoint existing Task
  Force Members,

  2. The Mayor would be granted a total of five (5) nominations for
  appointment to the Task Force, arguably holding the power to sway
  any recommendation made by said Task Force to the City Council
  on the new boundaries of individual Council Districts.  I
  recommended previously a more egalitarian process, as one of
  many potential models, allowing each Councilmember to have 2
  appointees to the Redistricting Task Force.

  3. The Charter Reform Committee specifically desired the elected
  Mayor have no more power than any one Councilmember, except
  with minor exception to set the Agenda, serve as the titular head of
  city government (exercising those powers attendant or inherent in
  that role) and possibly form certain committees, and so only the City
  Council can determine the process for considering members for the
  various Commissions and appointed bodies.

  4. The Redistricting Task Force is required by law and is not an
  instance where the Mayor is reposed singularly with the power to
  nominate five (5) of its members and to do would lessen the role of
  the City Council in shaping this process.

  5. The initial set of appointees to the Redistricting Task Force were
  required to fill out and submit an application for consideration which
  could be reviewed by the public and the City Council. At a minimum,

  appointment.
  6. There must be some articulation of the interests these additional
  appointees are intended to represent. Is it economic, racial,

  I would like staff to clarify where we are on the issue that the
  Councilmember just raised so we will all have a clear
  understanding."

  Mayor Gordo noted that he believes the issue is landmark status
  eligibility; whether there should have been a different level of review
  regarding that status and that is what he understands is the concern
  raised by Councilmember Williams.

  Mr. Reyes confirmed that if the proposed project was formally
  designated as a Landmark and the applicant submitted the current
  application for a Hillside Development Permit (HOP), staff's
  perspective would still be to approve the HOP.

  Councilmember Gordo expressed concerns with staff's lack of
  action in conducting a site visit to investigate the concerns raised
  by the neighbors related to the accessory structures at the back of
  the proposed project site, protected tree on her property, and view
  impacts, which he believes to be new evidence; and the lack of
  information on the property owner accepting the conditions of
  approval. He also spoke on the need to analyze the project with
  cumulative impacts in the context of potential landmark structure,
  which may also be considered new evidence.

  Councilmember Williams expressed concerns with making a
  decision related to CEQA, with the property potentially being eligible
  for landmark designation status, which may affect the accessory
  structures; and spoke in favor of upholding the BOZA's decision and
  disapproving the Hillside Development Permit, which she believes
  of all the unfavorable options, that is the best option.

  Motion:  Following discussion, it was moved by Vice Mayor Wilson,
  seconded by Councilmember Hampton, to close the public hearing:

  AYES:  Councilmembers Hampton, Kennedy, Madison,
  Masuda, Rivas, Williams, Vice Mayor Wilson, Mayor
  Gordo
  NOES:  None
